The fluid dynamics video considers an array of two NREL 5-MW turbines separated by seven rotor diameters in a neutral atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) flow.
The precursor ABL simulation was performed on a LES grid with dimensions of 3 km x 3 km x 1 km and a resolution of 15 m.
The turbine-array simulation used three layers of nested refined grids, with a resolution of about 2 m around the turbines and throughout the wake.
The tip vortices of the upstream turbine became unstable and broke down into larger turbulent structures after about 1.5 rotor diameters downstream.
The tip vortices of the downstream turbine broke down earlier due to the increased turbulence levels generated by the wake of the upstream turbine.
The power generated by the downstream turbine was significantly reduced compared to the upstream turbine, due to the momentum deficit in the upstream wake not fully recovering.
The precursor ABL simulation reached a quasi-stationary state after approximately 12,000 seconds of real time.
The research was supported by the Department of Energy Grant DE-EE0005481.
The fluid dynamics video was created using a data extract workflow with the FieldView CFD post-processing tool.
Intelligent Light provided the FieldView 14 software licenses, and Earl P. N. Duque from the Applied Research Group at Intelligent Light provided continuous support.
The actuator line method (ALM) was used to model the wind turbine blades by adding body forces to the momentum equation.
The neutral atmospheric boundary-layer flow data was obtained from the precursor ABL simulation using a Large-Eddy Simulation (LES) framework within OpenFOAM.
The fluid dynamics video shows the downstream advection of an iso-surface of vorticity magnitude (ω = 0.5 s^-1) and contours of velocity magnitude to illustrate the breakdown process of tip vortices.
The larger-scale turbulent structures break down into smaller-scale turbulence with distance from the upstream wind turbine.
The research aimed to enhance the physics-based understanding of wind turbine wakes.
